title: The default-deadline test monkeypatches the global Date.now and process.stderr.…
description:
The default-deadline test monkeypatches the global Date.now and process.stderr.write. Both are correctly restored in a finally block and bun runs a file's tests serially, so this is safe today, but a shared withFakeClock helper under test/helpers/ would make the pattern reusable and harder to leak if the test is ever copied.

Source: cam/issue-358
Review round: 2

suggestion-fingerprint: 3d29a2c5ace6

spec.scope: Extract the duplicated fake-clock monkeypatch idiom in test/dispatch.test.ts into a shared, callback-style helper test/helpers/with-fake-clock.ts, and migrate the two existing sites to use it. The helper saves the original Date.now and process.stderr.write, installs a fake clock (Date.now returns a mutable fakeNow starting at 0) plus a stderr.write that captures written chunks, invokes the caller's callback with an object exposing advance(ms) (advancing fakeNow) and the captured-chunks array, and restores BOTH globals in a finally block so restoration is guaranteed even if the callback throws. Migrate Site A (the sendKeysWhenIdle default-deadline test near line 316) and Site B (the CAM-373 idle-gate exactly-once test near line 720) to withFakeClock, preserving each site's distinct behavior. Add a dedicated helper test proving restore-on-throw. Test-only change: no production/sidecar-executed code and no templates/ touched, so NO coherence rebuild is required.
acceptanceCriteria: A new shared helper file test/helpers/with-fake-clock.ts exports a named withFakeClock function following the existing test/helpers convention (a `// test/helpers/with-fake-clock.ts` path-banner comment on line 1, a rationale docblock, named export only, no default export). [oracle: grep -q 'export function withFakeClock' test/helpers/with-fake-clock.ts]

withFakeClock is callback-style: it saves the original Date.now and process.stderr.write, installs a fake clock (Date.now returns a mutable fakeNow starting at 0) and a chunk-capturing process.stderr.write, invokes the caller's callback with an object exposing an advance(ms) function that advances fakeNow and the captured-chunks array, and restores BOTH globals in a finally block so restoration is guaranteed even when the callback throws. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

test/dispatch.test.ts imports the helper via `import { withFakeClock } from './helpers/with-fake-clock.ts';` (relative path, explicit .ts extension per file convention). [oracle: grep -qF "from './helpers/with-fake-clock.ts'" test/dispatch.test.ts]

Both former inline fake-clock sites in test/dispatch.test.ts (the sendKeysWhenIdle default-deadline test near line 316 and the CAM-373 idle-gate exactly-once test near line 720) are migrated to withFakeClock; the inlined monkeypatch idiom `Date.now = () => fakeNow` no longer appears anywhere in test/dispatch.test.ts. [oracle: ! grep -qF 'Date.now = () => fakeNow' test/dispatch.test.ts]

The migrated sites preserve their distinct pre-existing behavior: the default-deadline test still asserts the captured stderr contains the IDLE_WAIT_DEADLINE_MS deadline message and NOT the literal 5000 ms message; the CAM-373 idle-gate test still records sleeps via its own sleepFn (advancing the clock through the helper's advance) and still asserts send-keys fires exactly once. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
The dispatch test suite still passes unchanged after the refactor. [oracle: bun test test/dispatch.test.ts]

A dedicated helper test test/helpers/with-fake-clock.test.ts exists and passes, proving at minimum that withFakeClock restores both Date.now and process.stderr.write even when the callback throws (the leak-safety property motivating this refactor). [oracle: bun test test/helpers/with-fake-clock.test.ts]
gotchas: The two sites are NOT byte-identical: Site A (near 327) saves both originals contiguously and names its capture array `captured`; Site B (near 723) saves originalWrite first, then does test-specific setup, then saves originalNow, names its capture array `stderrChunks`, and also records sleeps in `recordedSleeps`. The finally restore block and the `Date.now = () => fakeNow` override are byte-identical at both. The helper must accommodate both usages: expose the captured array to the callback and let the caller's injected sleepFn advance the clock via advance(ms).

test/check-test-sleeps.test.ts references test/helpers/*.ts paths only as synthetic string FIXTURES passed to scanForSleeps (around lines 52 and 142); it is NOT an allowlist of real helper files, so the new helper needs NO registration there. The helper contains no real sleeps, so the sleep-scanner guard is unaffected.

Follow the existing test/helpers convention exactly (see flush-ink.ts, wait-for-condition.ts, mock-terminal-size.ts): path-banner comment on line 1, rationale docblock, named export only. The dispatch.test.ts import uses the relative ./helpers/<name>.ts form with explicit extension.

bun runs a file's tests serially, so the current inline pattern is safe today; the refactor's value is reusability + leak-safety if the idiom is ever copied, NOT fixing a live bug. Do not change dispatch behavior or existing assertions.
Test-only change: no templates/ and no sidecar-executed code (src/supervisor, src/tmux/dispatch.ts) is touched, so NO coherence rebuild is required after this ships.
domainTerms: withFakeClock: the new shared test helper that monkeypatches Date.now + process.stderr.write with guaranteed finally-restore.
fake-clock idiom: saving Date.now/process.stderr.write, overriding with a mutable fakeNow + chunk-capturing stderr, restoring in finally.
Site A / Site B: the two dispatch.test.ts tests using the idiom (sendKeysWhenIdle default-deadline near line 316; CAM-373 idle-gate exactly-once near line 720).
IDLE_WAIT_DEADLINE_MS: the exported default deadline the Site A test asserts against.
